section_summary: This section continues a report on Japanese wartime industrial control, then presents appendices on control societies, associations, corporations, and their governing laws. The examples cover metals, electrical equipment, warehouses, lumber, woolens, bicycles, and small businesses. The final appendices describe export associations, goods held for postwar trade, and the commodity link system.

people.name: Kichihiko Taniguchi
people.role: Professor and author of the cited study “The Link System in Japan”

subfiles.title: Report on Munitions Superintendence Bureaus
subfiles.about: The excerpt explains the bureaus’ organization and their relationship with munitions firms and other authorities.
subfiles.summary: It describes five bureau sections and considers overlapping authority involving company managers, local administrations, and Army and Navy factories. The report argues that shared production goals and personnel ease these tensions.

subfiles.title: Appendix V: Major Industries Organization Ordinance
subfiles.about: The ordinance establishes the powers, organization, and supervision of industrial control societies and associations.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance defines membership, officers, meetings, assessments, inspections, and penalties for Control Societies and district Control Associations. It gives ministers extensive approval, direction, and dissolution powers, with special provisions for military matters and overseas territories. A supplementary rule sets enforcement for September 1, 1941.

subfiles.title: Appendix VI: Amendments to the Essential Industries Organizations Law
subfiles.about: The amendments expand control associations’ administrative and commercial functions.
subfiles.summary: The amendments add planning, cooperative purchasing and marketing, accounting, worker welfare, inspection, and registration provisions, alongside changes concerning deputies and removal of officials.

subfiles.title: Appendix VII: Transfer of Administrative Authority Law
subfiles.about: The law transfers specified government permissions and allocation authority to control organizations.
subfiles.summary: An abstract assigns control bodies government authority and treats their orders and officials as governmental.

subfiles.title: Appendix VIII: Metal Industry Control Society
subfiles.about: The abstract describes the Metal Industry Control Society’s membership, committees, and plans for materials, labor, and production.
subfiles.summary: It outlines centralized control of metal goods, distribution of scarce materials, technical standardization, factory inspection, and labor planning. It also notes plans for metal supply in the South Seas.

subfiles.title: Appendix IX: Control Regulations for Hokkai Warehouse Enterprises
subfiles.about: The regulations specify reporting duties and control over warehouse operations, labor, storage, and fees.
subfiles.summary: Members must submit business and financial reports, obey directions on facilities and storage assignments, and accept association control of labor and rates.

subfiles.title: Appendix X: Electrical Engineering Control Society in Japan
subfiles.about: The abstract sets out the society’s purpose, powers, officers, and departments.
subfiles.summary: The society coordinates machinery production, allocation, resources, prices, and technical improvement from its Tokyo headquarters.

subfiles.title: Appendix XI: Electric Machine Control Society
subfiles.about: The abstract presents rules for governing the electric machine business and its control society.
subfiles.summary: Its articles cover membership, production and distribution control, officers, meetings, levies, dissolution, and fines. The society is directed by a ministerially appointed president.

subfiles.title: Appendix XII: Establishment of a Warehouse Control Society
subfiles.about: The abstract proposes a control society for warehouses at six major harbors.
subfiles.summary: It describes coordination with transportation bodies, control of warehouse property and essential goods, and measures to improve freight handling and protect stocks from air raids.

subfiles.title: Appendix XIII: Control of Electrical Engineering Industries
subfiles.about: The abstract proposes a control structure for thousands of electrical engineering firms.
subfiles.summary: It calls for regional companies, local associations, and a central society to coordinate labor, materials, and air raid duties.

subfiles.title: Appendix XIV: Regulations on Lumber and Charcoal Production
subfiles.about: The regulations give local governors control over timber cutting and charcoal production and sale.
subfiles.summary: Governors designate cutting, production, sale, shipping, and pricing terms for lumber and charcoal.

subfiles.title: Appendix XV: Pit Wood Control Association
subfiles.about: The abstract reports the creation of a pit wood association in Northern Kyushu.
subfiles.summary: The association supplies mine supports to coalfields and helps producers with transport costs and materials.

subfiles.title: Appendix XVI: Regulations of the Woolen Goods Control Society
subfiles.about: The regulations define the society’s authority over the woolen goods industry.
subfiles.summary: They cover production, distribution, prices, membership, officers, conferences, accounts, dissolution, and fines. The society’s headquarters are in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Appendix XVII: Japan Bicycle Control Society Regulations
subfiles.about: The regulations control bicycle manufacture, materials, inspection, distribution, and penalties.
subfiles.summary: Manufacturers require society permission and receive assigned materials and production quantities. The society directs distribution through affiliated associations and fines violations.

subfiles.title: Appendix XVIII: Essential Materials Supervision Corporation Law
subfiles.about: The law creates a government funded corporation to stockpile and manage essential materials.
subfiles.summary: The corporation may store, purchase, import, and sell materials under government plans, including reserves for emergencies.

subfiles.title: Appendix XIX: Small Scale Business Control Society Regulations
subfiles.about: The regulations describe control of small businesses in Tokyo and Osaka.
subfiles.summary: They specify membership, inspection, financial functions, officers, conferences, fees, dissolution, and fines under the Minister of Finance.

subfiles.title: Appendix XX: Middle and Small Scale Industries
subfiles.about: The abstract explains wartime reorganization of small and medium industries.
subfiles.summary: It gives figures for associations and limited companies, describes conversion toward munitions production, and contrasts voluntary industrial associations with compulsory Control Societies. It also outlines government restrictions on enterprise transfers and reorganization.

subfiles.title: Appendix XXI: Export Associations
subfiles.about: The abstract traces export associations and their wartime foreign exchange purpose.
subfiles.summary: It summarizes their growth, market coverage, overlap with industrial associations, and the 1937 commodity link system.

subfiles.title: Appendix XXII: Regulations Governing Special Responsibilities in Keeping
subfiles.about: The regulations authorize designated companies to buy and preserve miscellaneous goods for future exports.
subfiles.summary: They identify eligible goods, designated factories and companies, export destinations, raw material allocation, and ministry supervised committees.

subfiles.title: Appendix XXIII: The Commodity Link System in Japan
subfiles.about: The report explains how export performance was linked to permission to import materials.
subfiles.summary: It distinguishes import privilege and obligatory export systems, lists seven linked commodities, and describes cotton trade controls.
